newsitem.title: USA: Probe begun of PRRS-like illness in Iowa hogs.
newsitem.headline: Probe begun of PRRS-like illness in Iowa hogs.

text.p: Iowa agriculture officials on Monday confirmed the outbreak of a hog disease similar to Porcine Reproductive and Respiratory Syndrome (PRRS), a respiratory illness that sickens sows and newborn pigs.
"There are a few herds in southeast Iowa that may have a variant of PRRS that is not known now," said Jack Ratekin, information specialist with the Iowa Agriculture Department.
Hog operations affected were small- to medium-sized, with several thousand hogs possibly affected, Ratekin said.

He said sows in the affected herds were aborting in some cases and there appeared to be a higher morbidity in the sows than typically occurs with PRRS. Also, the illness is weakening and in some instances, killing newborn pigs.
"As far as I know, nobody's been in there and done any scientific work yet, it's just starting," Ratekin said.
Staff of the U.S. Agriculture Department's Animal Plant Health Inspection Service (APHIS) were investigating at the affected operations on Monday, he said.
"It's very localized and it's not very widespread," Ratekin said.
The National Pork Producers Council on Monday afternoon said it will hold a teleconference at 1530 CST with members of USDA's field team for an update on the situation.
